Maimed Cake

AreaGeometryConstructions
Game: This is a picture, not a game: a bite has been taken from one corner of the cake, and one straight cut shares what is left equally.
How to play: Drag the dots A, B, C and Z, or focus a dot and press the arrow keys. Use the boxes to change the cut and to show the guide lines and point names.
Look for the math

A small rectangle has been cut from one corner of a big rectangle. Surprisingly, one straight line can always give two people exactly the same area of what remains. Drag the inner point Z and watch the coloured pieces stay equal.

Start with the diagonal

Let the cake be the rectangle ABCD and let the missing piece be UZRD, with its sides parallel to the cake's. If Z lay on the diagonal BD, the cut BZ would already halve the cake: a diagonal splits a rectangle into two equal triangles, and the small corner is shared out the same way. Extend BZ until it meets the far edge at M — the right edge CD when Z is below the diagonal, the top edge AD when it is above. The dotted yellow line is this first attempt.

Add half a leftover rectangle

Through M draw the line parallel to the side the cut met. It reaches K on the opposite side and L next to Z. The leftover strip is AKLU (or KLRC in the other case). Choose Q so that ZQ = LU. The parallelogram idea behind Euclid I.43 gives Area(BZQ) = Area(AKLU) / 2: the triangle has the same base and height as the strip. Adding that triangle to the smaller side makes Area(piece 1) = Area(piece 2). The logic test confirms this for 3,144 configurations of the rectangle, Z and both cut modes, and also confirms the diagonal special case at 57 positions. The article's intermediate claim that BZ splits "KBCMZL" evenly is not literally right: M can lie above R, inside the removed corner. Below the diagonal, BZ splits the real cake part KBCRZL evenly into KBZL and BCRZ; the test checks the printed version and reports the difference.

A second, parallel cut

Slide the whole first cut by half the small vector: take BP = ZQ = LU / 2 (or RP = ZQ = RL / 2 above the diagonal). Then PQ is parallel to BZ, and it still halves the cake — the coloured areas in the status line stay equal. Uncheck “Parallel cut PQ” to see the triangle cut BQ instead.

Try this: drag Z from below the diagonal to above it. The dotted line switches from the right side to the top, but the two coloured pieces stay the same size.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
